paragraphs.title: The Status of Reuben, Judah, and Joseph

easy.q: Who was Israel’s firstborn by birth?

easy.explanation: The birthright was given to Joseph’s sons.
easy.q: To whom was the birthright given?

medium.q: Why was Reuben’s birthright not reckoned after him?

answers: Reuben received the throne, Judah the land, and Joseph the priesthood
Reuben was firstborn, Judah was leader, and Joseph received the birthright
All three received exactly the same honor
medium.explanation: The passage distinguishes birthright, leadership, and royal authority.
medium.q: How were the honors divided among the three brothers?

answers: Reuben was not counted according to the privileges of the firstborn
Reuben was not allowed to have children
Reuben’s name was removed from Israel

answers: They always belonged to the same person
They could be divided among different brothers
challenge.explanation: Joseph received the birthright, while Judah became the chief ruler.
challenge.q: What important distinction does the passage make between birthright and leadership?

answers: Leadership was not identical to the birthright
Judah became Reuben’s replacement as firstborn
Joseph and Judah were the same person
challenge.explanation: The verses separate Judah’s leadership from Joseph’s birthright.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Judah becoming the chief ruler while Joseph received the birthright?

challenge.explanation: The text says, “Judah prevailed above his brethren.”
challenge.q: Which word describes Judah’s superiority over his brethren?

answers: He was called prince of the Reubenites

easy.explanation: The Gadites dwelt in Bashan unto Salchah.

How many brethren are listed in the house of their fathers?

paragraphs.title: The Transjordan Tribes’ War against the Hagrites

answers: Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh
easy.explanation: These three groups are named as the warriors.
easy.q: Which tribes went to war together?

easy.explanation: They fought the Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab.
easy.q: Against whom did they make war?

answers: They took livestock and dwelt in the land
easy.explanation: They took cattle and dwelt in the captured territory.
easy.q: What did the tribes do after the victory?

answers: They cried to God and trusted in him
medium.explanation: They cried to God in battle and put their trust in him.

answers: A large force of trained warriors
medium.explanation: It was the number of men able to go to war.

The passage makes no connection between them

answers: The war ended without a result
The tribes lost all their livestock
challenge.explanation: The listed numbers show the abundance of the spoil.

paragraphs.title: Half of Manasseh, Its Sin, and Its Exile

easy.explanation: The text describes their territory from Bashan toward Hermon.
easy.q: Where did half the tribe of Manasseh dwell?

answers: Mighty men of valour and famous men
easy.explanation: They were mighty men of valour and famous men.
easy.q: How are the heads of Manasseh’s fathers’ houses described?

answers: They transgressed against God and worshiped the gods of the land
medium.explanation: They went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land.

answers: God stirred up the Assyrian kings to carry them away
medium.explanation: Their exile is presented as the result of their unfaithfulness.

answers: They violated their loyalty to God

The passage gives no connection between sin and exile
